direction.title: Performance program
direction.summary: Help a visitor compare scheduled performances. Put the program and the selected performance's time and practical details in one composition.

layout.skeleton: Pair a synopsis of the work with a program of selectable performances. Give each choice the same comparable facts and place the selected outcome beside the program.
layout.focus: An original close view of the decisive difference between the works, with a short plain-language description and a prominent selected performance.
layout.desktop: Use a strong title and a compact program next to the evidence from the selected work. Keep controls in reading order and the selected timetable close to its choice.
layout.mobile: At 390 × 844 px, show both choices with their decisive facts and the primary control before any decorative scene. Keep the updated choice and outcome together. Place the artwork within the comparison or just after it. Check enlarged text.
layout.rhythm: Group each performance's essential facts by aligned edges and shared rules. Give the selected work its own space instead of making every cover equally loud.

imagery.subject: Use original art or cleared assets to show the difference a visitor can use to choose. Keep a lightweight depiction immediately available, with a close detail when the decisive feature is small.
imagery.crop: Keep the decisive detail visible at desktop and phone widths. Retain any important timing or description as text.
imagery.fallback: Use a short factual description or labeled still when live art is unavailable. Keep all choices and journey information usable.

motion.trigger: Selecting a performance or an optional named detail
motion.effect: Update the chosen work and its details together. Animate the one visual change that communicates a difference.
motion.reduced: Show the final state immediately with the same labels and outcomes.

action.instruction: Show the decisive facts alongside every choice. If a constraint rules out the current choice, keep its selected row visible and mark why it no longer fits. State the viable alternative and what it gives up, and wait for the visitor to change selection. Keep the source of each estimate visible and recalculate from the supplied facts.
action.label: Use the supplied performance name

direction.why: Understand what makes a show worth choosing and see whether it fits the practical constraints in the same visit.

sources.observation: The tested wireframe view displayed the original on a full canvas with labeled controls separate from it. Keep the decisive evidence available while more elaborate art loads.
The review uses a direct call to action and fast access to the first useful result. Keep the program immediately operable while visitors compare shows.

direction.credit: Original program direction from the Counterweight study with independently observed FunTech and YC references.

interaction.focus: Use a two-tone focus ring (2 px paper with 2 px ink outside) on the primary control.
interaction.accent_role: Use the accent as a focal fill under accent_foreground. Check contrast before using it as text.
interaction.keyboard: Expose the primary control by keyboard and announce pending and completed states.

assumptions: Use only the project facts and assets in the brief.
sample_revised.handoff: Preserve the supplied facts and brand constraints. Use the palette and type as examples of hierarchy. For an unbranded brief, derive a visual identity from the specific subject and check contrast with the resulting colors. Let the artwork reveal what differs between the performances. Test the complete choice and recovery at 390 px, including focus, the visible reason a choice no longer fits, and the alternate's trade-off.

spec.task: You and another visitor want a shared-weight duet for up to £60 and need the 20:40 train. At each width and in each anonymous candidate, capture -before on first load. Locate the chosen duet, pair fare and explanation of shared weight. Tab to the option for a one-minute-longer walk and activate it. Verify that Hinge stays selected, arrives 20:31 and misses the assumed 20:30 buffer cutoff. By keyboard choose Call/Response and verify that 19:34 plus a nine-minute walk gives 19:43 with £48 for two. Capture -after. Restore the usual eight-minute walk and confirm 19:42 and visible focus. Capture -edge. If a required input or output is absent, report the specific absence. In the visual score name the visual mechanism, what it helps you understand about the two shows, and which part looks generic or hard to use. At opening, explicitly record whether both choices and their decisive facts are visible in the phone viewport before scrolling, then note whether the late alternative explains its choreography trade-off.
spec.brief: Build a creative page for Counterweight, a fictional dance festival. Two visitors want to choose a duet with shared-weight choreography for £60 or less and catch their 20:40 train. Hinge costs £60 for two, ends at 20:16, and shows joined hands carrying a mirrored counterlean. Call/Response costs £48 for two, ends at 19:34, and shows one gesture answering another without shared weight. Usual estimated walks to the station are 14 minutes from Hinge and 8 from Call/Response. Assume a ten-minute station buffer. Start with Hinge and usual walk selected. Let visitors choose either duet and toggle a one-minute-longer walk. Keep the chosen duet, exact pair fare, selected pace, estimated arrival, and buffer outcome visible and consistent. When Hinge misses the buffer, keep it selected and show that Call/Response still fits. Explain the decisive difference in choreography, using original artwork if useful. This is a preview with no payment.

calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout and misplaced focus after an invalid number
calibration.reason: Clear labels support the task, but the familiar layout offers limited originality and misplaced error focus impairs recovery.

primary_action.input: Tab to the extra-minute checkbox, press Space, Shift+Tab to Hinge, then ArrowDown.
primary_action.expected: Hinge remains selected and arrives at 20:31, missing the 20:30 buffer cutoff; Call/Response then arrives at 19:43 for £48 for two.
primary_action.observed: The checkbox kept Hinge selected and reported 20:31 and buffer missed. ArrowDown selected Call/Response; the interface reported a 19:34 end, nine-minute walk, 19:43 arrival and £48 for two.

A-1440.edge_observation: Tab and Space restored the usual eight-minute walk and 19:42 arrival. The checkbox had a visible yellow focus ring.
A-1440.fact_check: Hinge is £60 for two; its joined-hands mirrored counterlean shares weight. Call/Response uses answering gestures without shared weight. The displayed time arithmetic is consistent. The missed-buffer suggestion gives the alternative's timing but does not itself explain that choreography trade-off.
A-1440.strength: The large paired figures and changing colored illustration make the difference between a physical counterlean and answering gestures understandable.
A-1440.weakness: The oversized introduction and artwork push some of the result below the initial viewport; the small status panel is more generic than the illustration.
A-1440.repair: Reduce the hero height and bring the arrival result and the alternative's non-shared-weight trade-off closer to the choice.

primary_action.input: Tab to the extra-minute checkbox and press Space; Shift+Tab and ArrowDown select Call/Response.
primary_action.expected: Hinge remains selected at 20:31 with the buffer missed; Call/Response shows 19:43 and £48 for two.
primary_action.observed: Both transitions worked. Hinge showed 20:31 and buffer missed; Call/Response showed 19:34 plus nine minutes, 19:43 and £48 for two.

A-390.edge_observation: Tab and Space restored eight minutes and 19:42, with a visible yellow focus ring around the checkbox.
A-390.fact_check: On first load, neither complete choice nor its fare and end time is visible before scrolling. Hinge's shared-weight explanation is visible. The missed-buffer suggestion supplies the earlier arrival but does not itself explain that Call/Response gives up shared-weight choreography.
A-390.strength: The paired-figure illustration makes the selected show's connection legible and changes with the selection.
A-390.weakness: The large illustration and headline delay the actual comparison on a phone; the result requires scrolling.
A-390.repair: Place compact choice rows and decisive fare, choreography and timing facts before the large illustration.

primary_action.input: Tab to the usual-walk radio, press ArrowRight, Shift+Tab to Call/Response and press Space.
primary_action.expected: Hinge remains selected at 20:31 with the buffer missed; Call/Response then shows 19:43 and £48 for two.
primary_action.observed: The longer walk retained Hinge and reported 20:31 and buffer missed. Call/Response then showed a 19:34 end, nine-minute walk, 19:43 arrival and £48 for two.

B-1440.edge_observation: Tab and ArrowLeft selected the usual eight-minute walk and reported 19:42. A visible focus outline surrounded the selected walk option.
B-1440.fact_check: Both choices state their prices, end times and the distinction between shared weight and answering gestures. The displayed arithmetic is consistent. The choreography trade-off is stated in the alternative's choice row.
B-1440.strength: The selected yellow row and side-by-side descriptions make the two shows and their trade-off easy to compare.
B-1440.weakness: The large promotional hero and conventional plan panel make the station result less immediately visible; the circular slogan is decorative and generic.
B-1440.repair: Shorten the hero and move the plan's arrival and buffer status higher into the initial viewport.

primary_action.input: Tab to the usual-walk radio, ArrowRight for the longer walk, Shift+Tab to Call/Response and Space to select it.
primary_action.expected: Hinge remains selected at 20:31 with the buffer missed; Call/Response then shows 19:43 and £48 for two.
primary_action.observed: The longer walk retained Hinge and reported 20:31 and buffer missed. Selecting Call/Response reported 19:34 plus nine minutes, 19:43 and £48 for two.

B-390.edge_observation: Tab and ArrowLeft restored the eight-minute walk and 19:42. The usual-walk option had a visible focus outline.
B-390.fact_check: Before scrolling, both choices, their pair fares, end times and choreography descriptions are visible. Call/Response explicitly says the dancers do not share weight, explaining the trade-off. The station result is below the initial viewport.
B-390.strength: The contrasting selected row puts the two shows' choreography, prices and end times together in the first phone viewport.
B-390.weakness: The plan is separated from the choices by an additional illustration and requires scrolling to see the resulting arrival; the plan panel is visually conventional.
B-390.repair: Keep the comparison visible while moving a compact arrival and buffer summary immediately beneath the choices.

preference.reason: Both complete the keyboard flow, but B exposes both choices and their decisive fare, end-time and choreography facts in the initial phone viewport. A has the more distinctive movement illustration, while B makes the central trade-off easier to assess.

live.unsupported_claims: The reviews verify the interface's displayed prices, choreography descriptions and time arithmetic, not the real-world accuracy of the underlying show, fare, walk or train data.

spec.brief: Build a creative page for Glasshouse, a fictional chamber music festival. A visitor wants to hear bass clarinet and needs a step-free entrance. Reed and Glass starts at 18:15 in Atrium with bass clarinet and glass harp. The garden door is step-free. Night Reeds starts at 19:00 in Loft with bass clarinet and viola. The Loft entrance has five steps. Both recitals are free. Let the visitor choose either recital and see the instruments, start time, and entrance for their selection. Start with Reed and Glass selected and both choices visible. Include a Step-free entrances only filter. If the visitor chooses Night Reeds and enables the filter, explain that their choice has five steps and offer Reed and Glass for them to select. Turning the filter off must restore both choices. Keep the selected state, focus and entrance details clear even at 390 pixels. Use original artwork if useful. This is a preview.
spec.task: You want to hear bass clarinet and need a step-free entrance. Capture -before at the top before using the page. Identify which recital, start time, and entrance match, and whether the recital choices are immediately visible. Select Night Reeds by keyboard and verify its start and five entrance steps. Turn on the step-free filter by keyboard. Observe whether the conflicting choice is explained, whether its focus or selection changes, and whether the eligible 18:15 recital is offered. Choose that recital by keyboard and capture -after. Turn the filter off and capture -edge after checking that both choices return. Report visible focus and any invented access promises. Score the page and describe the concrete visual mechanism and whether it made the trade-off easier to understand. At the filter conflict explicitly say whether Night Reeds is still visible in the choice list with its selected state and a reason it fails the filter.

calibration.basis: A legible, familiar repair intake with clear labels is coherent and usable, but misplaced focus after an invalid number is a material interaction flaw.

primary_action.input: Tab to Night Reeds, Enter; Shift+Tab to the filter, Space; Tab to Reed and Glass, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Compare the selected recital with the step-free requirement and select the eligible recital.
primary_action.observed: Both choices were visible initially. Night Reeds selected at 19:00 with five entrance steps. Filtering preserved it in the selection panel but removed it from the choice list; a status explained the five steps and offered Reed and Glass. Focus remained on the filter, and Reed and Glass was selectable at 18:15. A yellow outline showed keyboard focus.

A-1440.edge_observation: Space turned the filter off and both choices returned, with Reed and Glass still selected. At the conflict, Night Reeds was not visible in the choice list with its selected state, although the status gave the reason it failed.
A-1440.fact_check: The page identifies Reed and Glass, 18:15, Atrium garden door as the bass clarinet and step-free match. Night Reeds is 19:00 in the Loft with five steps. No additional access promise was observed. Venue facts cannot be independently verified from the review views.
A-1440.strength: The large blue and yellow editorial composition and side-by-side selection panel give the programme a strong identity.
A-1440.weakness: Removing the selected choice from the list makes the conflict harder to reconcile, even though the explanation names it.
A-1440.repair: Keep Night Reeds visible and selected in the filtered list, with its five-step conflict adjacent to it.

primary_action.input: Tab to Night Reeds, Enter; Shift+Tab to the filter, Space; Tab to Reed and Glass, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Find and select the step-free bass clarinet recital by keyboard.
primary_action.observed: Both choices were visible at the top without scrolling. Night Reeds selected at 19:00 with five steps. The filter kept focus and the selection but removed Night Reeds from the list; the status explained the conflict and offered Reed and Glass at 18:15. The selected eligible card had a visible yellow focus outline.

A-390.edge_observation: Turning the filter off restored both choices. At the conflict, Night Reeds was not visible in the choice list with its selected state, although the status stated that it had five steps.
A-390.fact_check: Reed and Glass is shown at 18:15 with a step-free garden door; Night Reeds is shown at 19:00 with five Loft entrance steps. No additional access promise was observed. The venue facts are not independently verified.
A-390.strength: The stacked layout keeps both choices and the filter visible in the initial mobile viewport.
A-390.weakness: The selected recital's detail panel is below the choices, and the filtered list hides the conflicting selection.
A-390.repair: Retain the selected conflicting card with its reason inline, keeping the alternative immediately adjacent.

primary_action.input: Tab to Night Reeds, Enter; Shift+Tab to the filter, Space; Tab to Reed and Glass, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Understand the conflict and select the eligible recital without losing context.
primary_action.observed: Both choices were immediately visible. Night Reeds selected at 19:00 with five Loft entrance steps. When the filter was enabled, focus stayed on it and Night Reeds remained visibly selected in the choice list, labelled 'Selected · five steps'. A status explained that it did not match and offered Reed and Glass at 18:15. Enter selected the latter, with a visible focus outline.

B-1440.edge_observation: Turning the filter off restored both choices and retained Reed and Glass as selected. The conflict status sat below the cards and was partly below the initial desktop viewport, although the selected card itself stated the five steps.
B-1440.fact_check: The displayed match is Reed and Glass at 18:15, Atrium, via the step-free garden door. Night Reeds is 19:00, Loft, with five steps. No additional access promise was observed. The venue facts are not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: The yellow selected card preserves the user's choice beside the eligible alternative, with entrance and instrument details directly comparable.
B-1440.weakness: The full conflict explanation falls partly below the initial desktop viewport.
B-1440.repair: Place the conflict explanation directly beside or within the selected card so it is fully visible when the filter changes.

primary_action.input: Tab to Night Reeds, Enter; Shift+Tab to the filter, Space; Tab to Reed and Glass, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Understand the conflict and select the eligible recital by keyboard.
primary_action.observed: Both choices were visible initially. Night Reeds selected at 19:00 with five steps. Enabling the filter kept focus on the switch and kept Night Reeds visible and selected in the choice list, with 'Selected · five steps' and a visible explanation that it failed the filter. Reed and Glass at 18:15 remained available and was selected with Enter; the card showed a yellow focus outline.

B-390.edge_observation: Space turned the filter off and both choices returned, with Reed and Glass still selected.
B-390.fact_check: The page identifies the 18:15 Reed and Glass recital and step-free garden door as the match; Night Reeds is 19:00 with five Loft entrance steps. No additional access promise was observed. The venue facts are not independently verified.
B-390.strength: The selected yellow card, adjacent alternative and explicit conflict message make the trade-off legible in one mobile view.
B-390.weakness: The conflict card's entrance text wraps tightly beside its selection label.
B-390.repair: Give the entrance and selection status more horizontal room or stack the status beneath the entrance on narrow screens.

preference.reason: B keeps Night Reeds visibly selected alongside the step-free alternative and names the five-step conflict. Its aligned times, entrance details and yellow selected state make the trade-off easier to compare without losing the user's selection.
